bark verb

of a dog

also woof, woof woof, woof-woof, bow-wow, bow wow, bark at, barking

classical

Traupman 142
Traupman 277

lātrō, lātrāre

verb, first conjugation

Other words

  • * (our own formation) bau bau — woof woof

    interjection · also used · * our formation

    We have found no ancient interjection for a bark; bau is the sound in Lucretius’s baubārī (below).

  • baubor, baubārī — bark softly, bay

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Lucr. 5.1071 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx rāra: Lucr.)

    Of dogs left alone in an empty house; Lewis & Short sets it against lātrāre, to bark angrily.

  • allātrō, allātrāre, allātrāvī, allātrātum — to bark at

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 142; Lewis & Short: not before the Augustan age; Traupman 277

    Lewis & Short: not before the Augustan period, and then mostly of people, “to assail with harsh words”.

  • lātrātus, lātrātūs m. — a bark, barking

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 3.411: latrātū turbābis agēns (Lewis & Short); Traupman 142; Verg. G. 3.411 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 277

Examples

  • heus, inquit, linguam vīs meam praeclūdere, nē lātrem prō rē dominī?

    “Hey,” he said, “do you want to stop my mouth, so that I won’t bark to guard my master’s goods?”Phaedr. 1.23.5–6

  • Canis lātrat: bau bau!

    The dog’s barking: woof woof!composed

See also dog, yelp, howl.
